questions.prompt: What is motion?
questions.explain: Any time something's position changes, from a turning page to Earth circling the Sun, that is motion.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for speed?
questions.explain: Speed tells how far something goes in a certain amount of time.

questions.prompt: What are the SI units for speed?
questions.explain: Distance in meters divided by time in seconds gives meters per second.

questions.prompt: Motion is always described compared to a...
questions.explain: Whether something seems to move depends on what you compare it to, called a reference point.

questions.prompt: What is velocity?
wrong: How heavy a moving object is
questions.explain: Velocity is like speed, but it also tells which way something is going.

questions.prompt: What is acceleration?
questions.answer: The rate at which velocity changes
questions.explain: Any time velocity changes, the object is accelerating.

questions.prompt: What is another word for slowing down?
questions.explain: Deceleration is negative acceleration, which means the object is slowing down.

questions.prompt: You sit on a smoothly moving train. Compared to you, how does the empty seat next to you seem to move?
wrong: It seems to move very fast
questions.explain: You and the seat move together, so from your reference point the seat stays still.

questions.prompt: Earth spins very fast. Why don't we feel or see it spinning?
questions.answer: Everything around us moves along with us
questions.explain: We, the air and the buildings all spin together, so nothing seems to move compared to us.

questions.prompt: What is average speed?
wrong: The speed at one exact moment
questions.explain: Average speed looks at the whole trip, even if the speed changed along the way.

questions.prompt: A car's speedometer shows how fast it is going right now. What kind of speed is that?
questions.explain: Instantaneous speed is the speed at one particular moment.

questions.prompt: Which of these counts as accelerating?
questions.answer: Speeding up, slowing down or turning
wrong: Only moving in a straight line
Only coming to a full stop
questions.explain: Acceleration is any change in velocity, so changing speed or direction both count.

questions.prompt: A car turns a corner at a steady 20 km/h. What changes?
questions.answer: Its velocity, but not its speed
wrong: Its speed, but not its velocity
questions.explain: The speed stays the same, but the direction changes, so the velocity changes.

questions.prompt: What are the units of acceleration?
questions.explain: Acceleration is a change in m/s every second, which is written m/s².

questions.prompt: A dog runs 40 m in 8 s. What is its average speed?
questions.explain: Speed = distance ÷ time, so 40 m ÷ 8 s = 5 m/s.

questions.prompt: A bike travels 150 m in 10 s. What is its average speed?
A cat runs 30 m in 5 s. A rabbit runs 36 m in 4 s. Which is faster?
questions.explain: Cat: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 m/s. Rabbit: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 m/s. The rabbit is faster.

questions.prompt: A car moves at 20 m/s for 5 s. How far does it go?
questions.explain: Distance = speed × time, so 20 m/s × 5 s = 100 m.

questions.prompt: How long does it take to walk 60 m at a speed of 2 m/s?
questions.explain: Time = distance ÷ speed, so 60 m ÷ 2 m/s = 30 s.

questions.prompt: A skateboard speeds up from 2 m/s to 8 m/s in 3 s. What is its acceleration?
questions.explain: Acceleration = (final velocity - starting velocity) ÷ time = (8 - 2) ÷ 3 = 2 m/s².

questions.prompt: A bee flies in a circle at a constant speed. Is it accelerating?
questions.answer: Yes, because its direction keeps changing
wrong: No, because its speed stays the same
Yes, because its speed keeps rising
questions.explain: Changing direction changes velocity, and any change in velocity is acceleration.

questions.prompt: A runner's acceleration points opposite to the direction she is running. What is she doing?
questions.explain: Acceleration opposite to the motion is negative acceleration, or deceleration.
